about.title: Aliso Viejo Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Defective products don't announce themselves — a malfunctioning kitchen appliance, a car part that fails on Aliso Viejo Parkway, or a tool that breaks during normal use can turn an ordinary day into a trip to the emergency room. Aliso Viejo residents shop at the same retailers and use the same consumer goods as anywhere else in Orange County, and when something goes wrong, California law gives injured people a real path forward. Unlike many negligence cases, product liability claims here often rely on strict liability, meaning the focus is on the product's condition, not proving someone was careless. That said, these cases usually involve manufacturers, distributors, and sometimes retailers, each with their own insurers and defense strategies. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle your claim directly — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate what happened and explain your options under California law, all on a contingency basis so you owe nothing unless there's a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why This Matters Under California Law

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify the Path Forward
items.desc: California often lets injured people pursue a claim by showing a product was defective and caused harm, without having to prove the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which means an attorney may need to investigate the entire supply chain.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters Early On
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central evidence, keeping it unaltered and unrepaired can be important to how a claim develops.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. An independent attorney can review your situation to see whether this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, without repairing or discarding it. The product is often key evidence, and an attorney can advise on how to preserve it properly.

items.question: Are there specific spots in Aliso Viejo where this comes up more?
items.answer: Product-related injuries themselves aren't tied to any particular intersection, but corridors like Aliso Creek Road and Pacific Park Drive see notable collision activity, and some product-related vehicle failures surface in that context. Each case still depends on its own facts.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and the independent attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
